newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expected to name Ruff White House counsel.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to name Ruff White House counsel.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is expected to name lawyer Charles Ruff as White House counsel to replace Jack Quinn, who last month resigned for personal reasons, an administration official said Tuesday.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said Ruff's appointment as the top White House lawyer could be announced as early as Tuesday.

Ruff, a Washington lawyer, served as the Watergate special prosecutor from October 1975 through June 1977. He has also worked as the chief corporation counsel for the District of Columbia, the city of Washington's top lawyer.

Ruff, whom Clinton considered as a candidate for deputy Attorney General when he came to office in 1993, becomes Clinton's fifth White House counsel, following Bernard Nussbaum, Lloyd Cutler, Abner Mikva and Quinn.

The administration official said several other White House positions may also be announced on Tuesday, including the naming of deputy White House counsel Kathleen Wallman as the chief of staff on the National Economic Council.
Cheryl Mills, currently an associate White House counsel, was expected to be elevated to deputy counsel, the official added.
